sections.h2: Collecting and valuing: two different offices
sections.html:
Taxes are collected at 423 College Street, Room 401, by the Carroll County Tax Commissioner. Bill questions go to 770-830-5843. The tag and tax counter, at 770-830-5826, helps customers from 8 to 5 on weekdays and wraps up title transactions at 4:30.

Setting values falls to the Board of Tax Assessors, 770-830-5812. Here the assessors also take returns and homestead applications, unlike counties where the collector does. The tax commissioner neither assesses nor sets millage, and the rates come from the county commissioners and the school board.

  • Late interest, returned mail, a bill total: tax commissioner.
  • Value, exemption, return or appeal: assessors.
  • Copy of your warranty deed: Clerk of Superior Court, in the courthouse.

Paying by card adds 2.5%, at the counter or on the commissioner's website, and that fee goes to the processor.

sections.h2: Due date, late interest and penalties
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property are normally due December 1. Manufactured homes run on April 1, and vehicle tax falls due on the owner's birthday. A check in the mail counts when it bears a United States Postal Service postmark; a postage-meter stamp is not accepted. The statement is mailed to the owner, never the mortgage company, so if your lender escrows, give them your copy.

Late balances pick up interest monthly at the bank prime loan rate plus 3%. After 120 days a 5% penalty attaches, and it recurs every 120 days until it totals 20%. Homestead accounts under $500 do not face that penalty.

sections.h2: Why settle a Carroll County lien before listing?
sections.html:
Once 120 days have gone by, the commissioner can file a tax FiFa with the Clerk of Superior Court. The filing is public, credit bureaus can read it, and the office cannot control how they use it. Failing payment, the commissioner may levy on the house, though the office describes that as a last resort.

Carroll also holds tax sales, where bidders must show up with cash, certified funds or a bank letter. Your house does not have to end up there. When you sell, the title company requests a payoff, prints it on the settlement statement and pays the county from your proceeds, so nothing reaches the courthouse steps.

Assessment notices must go out by July 1. Your written appeal is due within 45 days of the notice date, and once that window closes the right is gone. Each notice shows fair market value, assessed value and a tax estimate based on last year's millage.

Filing means choosing among three tracks. One is the Board of Equalization, with a later appeal to Superior Court. Another is arbitration, which gives up Superior Court. The third is a hearing officer for non-homestead parcels worth more than $1 million, and it keeps Superior Court rights.

  • Accepted grounds: taxability, value, uniformity with similar parcels.
  • Rejected: a claim that the levy itself is too high.
  • The math: fair market value times 40%, less exemptions, times the millage rate.

sections.h2: Programs that end when the house sells
sections.html:
To count for this year, a homestead application must reach the assessors before April 1, with the warranty deed if you are applying for the first time. Once approved, it carries on by itself until you move or the deed changes.

Carroll County relief for older owners
ProgramWho qualifiesWhat a sale does
Elderly school tax exemptionAge 62 or older, net income of $10,000 or lessEnds when title changes
General exemptionAge 65 or older, same income capEnds when title changes
Tax deferralAge 62 or older, household income of $15,000 or lessDeferred tax becomes payable

Under a deferral the tax stays on the property until it changes hands or climbs to 85% of fair market value. A sale therefore makes the full amount payable out of your proceeds.

Two farm programs rest on a 10-year promise made to the assessors: farmland taxed at 30% of fair market value, and conservation-use land taxed by its present use. Before listing acreage under either one, ask the assessors how a sale affects the covenant.

Several more exist, each with strings attached that a buyer may care about. A building on the Georgia or National Register of Historic Places can qualify for preferential assessment on the structure and up to two acres around it, once the Department of Natural Resources certifies it as rehabilitated or landmark historic property.

Brownfield property enrolled in the state's Hazardous Site Reuse and Redevelopment Program can see its taxable assessment effectively frozen for ten years during cleanup. Forest land conservation use needs a 15-year covenant and tracts above 200 acres, and the house on that land does not get the break.

  • Mobile homes: file a return and obtain a location permit, with the current year's tax paid in full first.
  • Real and personal property returns can be filed with the assessors from January 1 to April 1.
  • If you file a new return stating a different value, your appeal rights survive another change by the board.

On the Alabama line in west Georgia, Carroll spans 499 square miles of land. Carrollton is the seat and largest city, and the rest of the municipalities are Villa Rica, Temple, Bowdon, Mount Zion, Whitesburg and Roopville. Interstate 20 runs across the north end. Population reached an estimated 131,036 in 2025, from 119,148 in the 2020 census.

Between 2020 and 2024 an owned home had a median value of $255,100 and rent a median of $1,153. Of 44,106 households, 71.3% own, and 1,065 building permits were issued in 2025.

sections.h2: What a seller's year looks like
sections.html: Winter and early spring are filing season: returns and homestead go to the assessors by April 1. Summer brings assessment notices, mailed by July 1 at the latest, and your 45-day appeal clock starts the day a notice is dated. Autumn ends with the December 1 payment. A sale in the middle of that cycle does not wipe out the year's bill, so plan the closing around it and let the settlement statement show who pays what.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
Get a written total from the tax commissioner, with any interest included. Ask the assessors to confirm your homestead exemption is on file and that the name on record matches your deed. If any acreage sits under a covenant, raise that with the assessors before you sign anything.

Give the payoff to the closing agent early. A cash buyer wants the same paperwork as a financed one, and the payoff letter lets the county release its claim when the deal closes. If your lender received the bill instead of you, ask them for a copy so the figures agree.

faqs.q: When do Carroll County property taxes come due?
faqs.a: December 1 covers real estate and business personal property, and manufactured homes are due April 1. Check the date printed on your statement.

faqs.q: What does lateness add to a Carroll County bill?
faqs.a: Interest builds monthly at the bank prime loan rate plus 3%. A 5% penalty starts at 120 days and repeats every 120 days up to 20%, except on homestead accounts under $500.

faqs.q: Is there a fee for card payment in Carroll County?
faqs.a: Yes, 2.5%, charged at the counter and online alike. It goes to the payment processor, not the county. Ask the commissioner's office about other ways to pay.

faqs.q: Does the Carroll County Tax Commissioner set my tax?
faqs.a: No. The commissioner bills what the assessors' values and the millage rates produce. Rates come from the county commissioners and the school board, and value questions go to 770-830-5812.

faqs.q: What is the Carroll County homestead cutoff?
faqs.a: April 1, at the Tax Assessor's Office, 423 College Street. A late application counts for the next tax year, and first-time applicants should bring their warranty deed.
